Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Owner-streamed values

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Context carried by a reliable action

Use owner streams when an authenticated participant produces observations, such as a Godot solver pose, that the authority accepts into replayable state. State(Value) stores entity ownership, current value, sample frontiers and pending handoff in ordinary replayable world state. Sample(Value) is an external observation; the library never invokes a physics solver during replay. Rules(Value) supplies immutable validation policy outside the saved state.

Odin
owned.init(&body, object_key, epoch, tick, initial_owner, initial_pose, rules)
owned.offer(&body, next_owner, tick, timeout_ticks)
result := owned.accept(&body, authenticated_sender, sample, tick, rules)
// result.transferred identifies the tick that commits the prepared owner.

An object key includes kind, slot and generation. Epoch/revision scopes fence old authority and ownership messages. Owner zero denotes no active producer; nonzero owner IDs are mapped by the application to authenticated senders. A sample carries no sender identity of its own. Nonempty samples require a sequence; exact duplicates do not mutate state, changed values at the same sequence conflict, and older scopes/ sequences or decreasing producer ticks are rejected.

An offer reserves a new revision and a complete preparation baseline. The old owner remains accepted until the first valid sample for the proposed revision commits at an authority tick. Cancel/expiry burn the reserved revision. cut explicitly changes the complete value/owner and advances its discontinuity marker; bind_epoch preserves value and owner while invalidating prior scopes and pending offers. Overflow never wraps a revision. These primitives do not elect/fence a legitimate session authority.

valid checks structural state and value constraints. sample_valid additionally accepts a canonical zero sample as an empty upstream control slot. Values containing references are rejected. Pose2 and Pose3 include position, rotation, linear and angular velocity and sleeping state. Limit validators reject nonfinite/out-of-bounds values, excessive velocity norms and non-unit 3D quaternions. A transition predicate may impose additional game constraints; it cannot prove an untrusted solver was honest.

Driver lives outside world state. drive selects Observer/Owner/Preparing from authority-observed state, local identity, live epoch and connection eligibility. It reports reseeds separately from cuts. Preparing → Owner retains the same revision and local solver; a fresh producer rebases sequence/tick counters from accepted state. capture cannot publish from an observer. Producer ticks order that producer's lineage; accepted_at is the authority's history timestamp.

The Godot Body2 and Body3 adapters supply actual rigid/character handling. The profile design and separate Replay Slopball describe integration and the tested configurations. This supports cooperative trust models. It does not make Godot contact solving deterministic, provide competitive anti-cheat, or turn live engine casts into historical collision queries.

Context carried by a reliable action#

Action_Context(Value) carries a producer value plus its ownership scope. capture_context(&driver, value) requires a committed Owner role and leaves the pose sequence/producer clock unchanged. read_context(&state, authenticated_sender, claim, authority_tick, rules) validates the current owner, exact object/epoch/ revision, time and value bounds, then returns the value without mutating state. It cannot accept a pending ownership offer or advance a stream frontier.

Use this when a reliable interaction must retain the caller's pose even if its unreliable movement observation is delayed, or a newer pose overtakes the command. The outer action supplies sequencing/deduplication. Scope changes fence old claims; new samples in the same scope do not. Rules.transition is a stream update policy and is not invoked by context reads. The game must explicitly select range, leash or age constraints appropriate to its trust model. A context has no authority history timestamp and does not certify an honest engine result.

Owner Cavecrawl uses this for original-style issued-position interactions and a 64-pixel throw-origin leash, while preserving current replicated avatar positions.
